title: Meadow pacing fix: cap snapshot renders per frame gap, honest after-batch readback marker, builds fill the cap, frame-free first build
context: Root cause confirmed 2026-10-13: Impeller's RenderTargetCache (keep-alive 4) evicts every per-frame offscreen target when 5 or more Picture.toImage/toImageSync renders happen between two frames. The Meadow renders about 155 snapshots per build (up to 36 in one frame gap) and its pacer marker (picture.toImage(1,1)) is itself a snapshot that resolves at raster encode rather than GPU completion. On Windows ANGLE the evicted targets are freed late: 14.6 GB video memory, frames of 100-300 ms, out-of-memory crashes on open and in onboarding. Android emulator: about 20% frame-rate loss per frame over the cap; onboarding 38-41 fps. Lab A/B with runtime switches on the Android emulator, macOS VM and the owner's Windows PC (seeded 6,838 days / 23,939 entries) compared marker kinds, the cap, build allowance policies and a frame-free first build.
options: Cap of 4 per gap + after-batch readback marker, estimate-paced builds (first prototype)
Cap + before-and-after markers, builds at half a frame of GPU
Cap + after-batch marker, cap alone sizes recolour and builds
Cap + after-batch readback marker; recolour estimate-paced; builds fill the cap while frames flow, held by unanswered markers; first build frame-free with 8-frame GPU batches and half-frame UI limit
option_reasons: Windows runs out of memory on onboarding and takes 13-17 s or crashes on open; Android onboarding 38-41 fps

Fixes Windows and Android onboarding but Android first scene +370 ms and macOS VM sharpen 2.37 s vs 0.90 s because the after-batch estimate includes the in-flight frame and shrinks builds to 1 step per frame
Precise GPU estimate, but on OpenGL two readbacks drain the GPU twice per batch and recolour packs 2.7 pieces per frame: Android onboarding 48.8 fps, p90 42-44 ms, no better than baseline
Same drain cost on OpenGL; macOS VM sharpen 1.37 s, no better than the chosen option
Overloads saturated GPUs during continuous recolour: macOS VM onboarding 19.9 fps vs 21.6 baseline

Chosen: Windows 4K first scene 552-567 ms, sharpen 1.47-1.54 s, 6.9 GB peak, onboarding 55 fps with no crash; Android first scene 631-640 ms vs 699, sharpen 1.43-1.58 s vs 1.40, onboarding 55-56 fps vs 41; macOS VM onboarding 26 vs 22.4 fps, sharpen 1.28 s vs 0.85 s (cap-bound at 60 Hz, smoother frames)
outcome: Chosen the last option. The four-snapshot cap is an engine invariant, not a device tuning; GPU feedback stays live (readback at GPU completion), recolour keeps the estimate-based share, builds use the cap as their per-frame limit with marker backpressure, and the first build runs without frames because nothing is on screen to protect. Remaining cost: on 60 Hz slow-GPU devices the sharpen after the first scene can land up to about 0.4 s later than today, with smoother frames throughout; it halves on 120 Hz displays.
